outcome: Informed consent processes (inducing labour, vaginal examinations, fetal monitoring, Syntocinon, caesarean)
cohort: A state-wide sample of 2,802 women in Queensland, Australia, who had recently given birth.
finding: Public Midwifery Continuity Care was associated with less scheduled caesareans, more unassisted vaginal births, better informed consent, less perineal trauma, less anxiety, and shorter postpartum hospital stays, while Private Obstetric Care was linked to more labour inductions and scheduled caesareans, with both Public Midwifery Continuity Care and Private Obstetric Care reporting highest quality interpersonal care.
mod_finding: Women in Public Midwifery Continuity Care were less likely to have a scheduled caesarean and more likely to have an unassisted vaginal birth, whereas women in Private Obstetric Care were more likely to have their labour induced and a scheduled caesarean birth, and less likely to experience unassisted vaginal birth.
cross-section timing: Data was collected in 2012 from women who had recently given birth.
